summary: Virgil I Grissom Municipal Airport (BFR) is a small general aviation airport serving Bedford, Indiana, in the southern part of the state. It is named after Virgil I. "Gus" Grissom, one of NASA's original Mercury Seven astronauts, who grew up in nearby Mitchell, Indiana. The airport primarily supports recreational flying, flight training, and corporate access to the limestone-producing region.
faqs:
Q: Who is the airport named after?
A: The airport honors Virgil I. "Gus" Grissom, one of NASA's Mercury Seven astronauts and the second American to fly in space. He was raised in nearby Mitchell, Indiana, and tragically died in the 1967 Apollo 1 fire.

Q: What type of aircraft use this airport?
A: BFR primarily serves general aviation traffic, including single-engine private planes, flight training aircraft, and occasional corporate or charter flights. It is not served by commercial airlines.

Q: Are there rental cars available at the airport?
A: Rental car availability is limited; visitors typically arrange vehicles in advance through local agencies in Bedford or drive from the airport.

Q: Does the airport have an air traffic control tower?
A: As a small municipal airport, BFR generally operates without a staffed control tower, and pilots use the common traffic advisory frequency for coordination.
transport_tips: Since BFR has no scheduled commercial service, arriving visitors will need a car—most travelers drive the short distance into Bedford from the airfield. The airport is conveniently located just a few miles from downtown Bedford, easily reached by local roads. Taxi and rideshare options can be sparse, so arranging ground transportation in advance is recommended.
local_tip: Bedford is known as the 'Limestone Capital of the World,' and visitors interested in local heritage should check out the nearby Limestone Heritage Trail, which showcases the quarries that built many of America's most famous monuments, including the Empire State Building and the Pentagon.
